Issued at 446 AM EDT Sun Sep 13 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Generally westerly flow aloft across the CONUS...between a PacNW 
upper low and ridging over the SW US (amplifying northward into the 
Intermountain West ahead of said upper low)...with 100-120kt upper 
jet stretched across the northern tier of the CONUS aiding in some 
Pacific moisture transport. Broad upper low swirls over the east-
central portion of Canada, with energy digging through 
Manitoba/Saskatchewan and swirling across Ontario. Shortwave 
troughing even digs as far south as the Upper Great Lakes/OH Valley, 
picking up cutoff energy over KY. Deepest moisture (pwats 1.5in or 
greater) over the central Plains into the Lower MS Valley where some 
convection is ongoing; otherwise, the rest of the deep moisture is 
being swept eastward ahead of a cold front stretching from OK to 
Saginaw Bay to northern Quebec. 1022mb surface high oozing into the 
Plains, with northwest flow aloft over the Great Lakes as a tight 
thermal gradient slips in...850mb temps falling from the teens over 
southern MI to 4C near the northern coast of Lake Superior, denoted 
by a second cold front draped across Ontario at 3z; 0C and colder 
airmass to our north over northern Manitoba and Ontario, though not 
sure that current trajectories support this kind of cold for us. 

Lobe of PV swings across the Upper Great Lakes today, with some 
showers, potentially lake effect/enhanced on WNW to NW flow, fading 
with time going into tonight as energy moves past and winds begin to 
diminish, though overlake instability will remain as ridging builds 
in quickly overnight tonight, resulting in a chilly night. The PacNW 
upper low tracks eastward across the northern Plains tonight into 
Monday, resulting in an increase in moisture transport through the 
Upper Midwest Monday night into Tuesday...and potential for heavy 
rainfall...as a boundary drapes into the area and stalls out to our 
south somewhere in the OH Valley. This could become problematic for 
the middle and latter portion of the week...as energy again tries to 
cut off across the PacNW/Intermountain West while the more 
progressive northern stream drags some energy across southern 
Canada, and perhaps the Upper Great Lakes, sometime in the Wednesday 
night-Thursday timeframe. Quite a bit of uncertainty beyond this for 
next weekend...but there are signals for the second bit of troughing 
in the PacNW to eject eastward, which could result in continued 
active weather across the eastern half of the country. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Lows tonight...With the cold air mass coming in today, and most of 
the area stuck in the 60s for highs...still have concerns some of 
the typical cold spots in the interior could drop down into the mid 
30s tonight as high pressure builds in...given incoming air mass is 
dry, perhaps even a smidgen drier than recent cooler air masses. 
Potential sticky wicket is lingering overlake instability and some 
potential for a smidgen of low-level moisture to hang on...which 
could be in the form of some cloud cover that could slow radiational 
cooling, though not sure how extensive this idea will be. We may 
also be a bit slower to settle down compared to points west, where 
the surface high will move in quicker, which could also slow 
radiational cooling. Have trended lows a little cooler for tonight 
especially across the interior higher terrain, down into the upper 
30s there...where a 25 degree temperature swing would take lows 
tonight down into the mid thirties. 

Heavy rain potential Monday night into Tuesday...Not a ton of change 
in the overall setup. Strong southwesterly flow ahead of the next 
system, combined with an increase in absolute moisture, will result 
in anomalous moisture transport into the Upper Midwest. 
Attm...signals point toward the most anomalous (beyond climo) 
moisture transport occurring to our west over WI Monday into Monday 
night, where there is a greater shot at weaker stability that could 
produce a better bang for our QPF buck; this area would also be more 
favored for heavy rain in a Maddox synoptic type setup, to which 
Monday night is somewhat similar. Expect we will see stronger 
frontogenetic responses that will enhance QPF in localized 
swaths...some of which are currently progged to influence the EUP 
and Tip of the Mitt region late Monday night...and will watch for a 
potential maximum in QPF up here, as well as elsewhere along the 
front (including the Saginaw Bay region in the afternoon/evening). 
Abundant moisture present in this setup is not favorable for typical 
instability parameters, but think we could still see some convective 
elements develop along a potential dry slot sweeping through 
Tuesday. Things appear to become more progressive here late Monday 
night into Tuesday as the PV max tracks relatively quickly across
